description: The merge phase currently treats ANY non-zero `git rebase` exit as a REBASE-CONFLICT: `engine/driver.sh` runs the rebase, and on failure captures `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` and aborts (the ~L346 `rebase_or_note` path). But a rebase can exit non-zero for reasons that are NOT a content collision — a dirty/locked worktree, a git refusal ('cannot rebase: you have unstaged changes'), a leftover `rebase-merge`/`MERGE_HEAD` state, or a config/ownership error — in which cases `--diff-filter=U` reports ZERO conflicted files. This was observed in the field: three talos branches strictly ahead of main (main an ancestor, so a rebase is a genuine no-op) were all labelled REBASE-CONFLICT with 'git reported none' conflicted files, blocking merges that had no real conflict. This tasklist teaches the merge phase to distinguish a REAL content conflict (≥1 `--diff-filter=U` path) from a rebase that was REFUSED for another reason, and to report/handle each correctly — so a dirty or locked worktree does not masquerade as a merge conflict. Scope: `engine/driver.sh` (the rebase/merge phase) + its test.

userStories.title: Distinguish a refused rebase from a real content conflict
userStories.description: At the rebase failure point in `engine/driver.sh`, a non-zero exit with zero `--diff-filter=U` paths is NOT a content conflict — it is a refusal (dirty/locked worktree, leftover rebase/merge state, ownership/config). Classify the two and label them distinctly.
acceptanceCriteria: When `git rebase <base>` exits non-zero AND `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U` lists ≥1 path, the outcome is still reported as REBASE-CONFLICT exactly as today (no regression to the real-conflict path)

When it exits non-zero with ZERO conflicted paths, the outcome is reported as a distinct state (e.g. REBASE-REFUSED / not a content conflict) whose message names the likely cause (unstaged/uncommitted changes, a leftover `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply`/`MERGE_HEAD`/`CHERRY_PICK_HEAD` state, or dubious-ownership) rather than 'conflict with git reported none'
The rebase is still aborted cleanly and the branch is left exactly as the agent left it (attached, un-rebased) in BOTH cases — this story changes the classification + message, not the safety behavior

A pre-flight check detects the obvious refusal causes (a dirty worktree, or a leftover rebase/merge state dir under the git-dir) before attempting the rebase, so the common case is diagnosed rather than inferred from a bare non-zero exit

userStories.title: The snapshot/note reflects the true cause
userStories.description: The `.rebase-conflict.md` snapshot the merge phase writes should not assert a content collision when there was none.
acceptanceCriteria: For a refused (non-content) rebase, the written operator note states it was a refusal and names the cause + the fix (e.g. clean/commit the worktree, clear the leftover rebase state), instead of the content-conflict resolution steps
For a real content conflict, the existing snapshot content (conflicted files, colliders, 'resolve inside the rebase' guidance) is unchanged

A strictly-ahead branch (base is an ancestor → rebase is a no-op) is never reported as either a conflict or a refusal — it rebases cleanly and proceeds to merge (this is the exact field case that motivated the tasklist)

userStories.title: Regression test for the spurious conflict
userStories.description: Pin the distinction with a hermetic test alongside the existing suite.
acceptanceCriteria: A hermetic test asserts: a branch with a REAL content conflict against a moved base is reported REBASE-CONFLICT with the conflicted files; a branch whose rebase is REFUSED by a dirty/locked worktree (zero `--diff-filter=U` paths) is reported as the distinct refusal state, not a conflict; and a strictly-ahead branch merges with no conflict/refusal at all
The test is hermetic (scripted fake provider on PATH, temp `CHIEF_*` prefixes) and joins the behavioral subset the verify hook + CI run
